resources.string: Use voice typing
Off removes the microphone from the whole keyboard

When this is off, the keyboard never opens the microphone. The Voice tool goes from the toolbar, the toolbox and the shortcuts, the boxes of the keyboard itself lose their microphone button, and the collapsed bar does not show. The recognition engines and the Whisper models are not loaded, so voice typing uses no memory. Your voice settings stay as they are for when you turn it on again.
Languages
Recognition engine

Dictation uses the first engine on this list that is on and can run on this phone. A language can still have an engine of its own, under Engine for each language. The first transcription server on the list is the one those languages send their clips to. If nothing on the list can run, the phone\'s recognizer is used.
How the keyboard turns speech into text

The system recognizer is fast and shows the words while you speak, but it depends on the operating system and its languages. Offline Whisper runs fully on your device across many languages and sends no audio anywhere. It transcribes each phrase after you stop speaking. Offline Whistle works the same way with one small, fast model for seven languages: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Polish. Offline Asr4All is English only, and writes the words while you speak, on your device. Offline Parakeet transcribes 25 European languages and works out which one you speak. Offline Moonshine is a small, quick model for English. A transcription server does the same work on a computer you choose, so your phone spends less battery. The recording of each phrase goes to that server and nowhere else.

Voice typing view
What the microphone button opens

The panel gives large controls and status in the space of the keyboard. The compact bar speaks over the keys, so you can correct words as they land. The collapsed bar hides the whole keyboard behind a small pill that you can drag anywhere, and it stays until you bring the keyboard back. The panel and the compact bar have a collapse button, and the pill has an expand button, so you can switch styles without coming back to this screen.

Voice typing mode
How voice typing and the keys share the field
The other modes need the voice typing view set to %1$s

One block at a time is the usual way. The words appear in the field while you speak, and the first key press stops the microphone.

Type while you speak keeps the microphone open. Each phrase goes into the field when you stop for breath, so the keys, the layouts and the suggestion strip stay live all through the session. Use it with the compact bar over the keys. This mode always keeps listening.

Plain text works the same way, but it adds no punctuation and no spaces. You control all of them from the keyboard. Use it for code, for terminals and for any field where you want only the words you said.

The two type-while-you-speak modes need the keys on screen, so they are offered only when the voice typing view is the compact bar over the keys. Plain text also needs the system recognizer: the offline models and a transcription server add their own punctuation.

Stop after a pause
End a Whisper or server clip by itself when you stop talking

Offline Whisper and the transcription server record a whole clip, so the microphone stays open until you press it or the clip fills: 30 seconds, or two minutes for a whisper.cpp model. Set a pause here and the clip ends by itself once you have said something and then gone quiet for that long. Asr4All, Sherpa and Omnilingual hear the pause with the Phrase end detector. With Keep listening off, that also ends dictation, so you never have to reach for the microphone. The system recognizer stops after a pause of its own and ignores this. Off by default.
Off

Reduce background noise
Clean up the microphone before an offline model hears it

Takes background sound such as traffic, a busy café or a fan out of the microphone\'s audio before an offline engine (Whisper, Whistle, Asr4All, Parakeet, Moonshine, Sherpa, Omnilingual) hears it. Light is RNNoise, a tiny network that adds about 10 ms. Strong is DPDFNet, a DeepFilterNet model on ONNX Runtime: a 9 MB download, more work for the phone and 40 ms of delay, but it is the one that helps recognition. On noisy test recordings Light cost Whisper words, and Strong won some back. Without its model, Strong runs as Light. The system recognizer and the transcription server get the microphone as it is. Off by default.

Phrase end detector
How Asr4All, Sherpa and Omnilingual hear that you stopped talking

Asr4All, Sherpa and Omnilingual write while you speak, so they listen for the end of what you say themselves: that is when Stop after a pause counts, and where Omnilingual cuts its phrases. Silero VAD is a small network that tells speech from other sound; every Sherpa and Omnilingual model carries a copy, and Asr4All can download one. FireRedVAD is a newer network that its makers measured ahead of Silero in 102 languages, with far fewer false alarms; a 2.3 MB download. Loudness only uses no model at all: anything loud enough counts as speech, the way the pause stop works for Whisper and the server, so a noisy room can keep it listening. Your own model takes a Silero or TEN VAD file. A detector that cannot run yet falls back to Auto, which is Silero where it can run and loudness everywhere else.

Speech threshold
Lower hears softer speech, higher stops sooner in noise

How sure the detector must be that a moment is speech. Lower keeps listening through soft or distant speech, but noise can hold the phrase open. Higher ends the phrase sooner in a noisy room, but a quiet voice can be taken for silence. For Loudness only it sets how loud counts as speech: 50% is the level the pause stop has always used. 50% by default.
Smart Turn
End sooner when you sound finished, wait longer when you do not

At each pause, Smart Turn v3.2 listens to the last 8 seconds and judges whether you finished what you were saying or stopped mid-thought, from how you said it: the falling voice at the end of a sentence, a word left hanging, an \"um\". When you sound finished, the phrase ends after a short pause; when you do not, it waits out the whole pause set in Stop after a pause. So you can set a long pause and still not wait at the end of every sentence. It was trained on 23 languages and is an 8.7 MB download that runs on ONNX Runtime. Off by default.

Add punctuation and capitals
Full stops, commas, question marks and capitals for Sherpa and Omnilingual

Sherpa and Omnilingual write the words they hear and nothing else: no full stops, no commas, no capitals. With this on, a punctuation model reads each finished phrase on the phone and puts in full stops, commas and question marks in the marks of the language (। in Bengali and Hindi, ؟ in Arabic, 。 in Chinese), with a capital at the start of every sentence. Names get their capitals from the keyboard\'s word lists, and English ones also from Sherpa\'s English punctuation model when you have it. The model knows 88 languages and is a 151 MB download; English works without it if the English model is on the phone. Engines that punctuate for themselves are never touched, nor is plain voice typing.

Words to listen for
Listen for my words
Names and other words from your dictionary, so they are spelled your way

Each time you dictate, the keyboard sends a list of your own words with it: the words you added by hand, the words in Android\'s personal dictionary, and the words the keyboard learned from your typing that are not in any word list, such as names. The system engine also gets permission to use what it knows about your phone, such as your contacts. The list goes to the engine that listens to your voice, and nowhere else. The system engine uses it on Android 13 and later, if the engine supports it. A transcription server gets it as part of its prompt, Offline Whistle as words to favour, the whisper.cpp models of Offline Whisper as their prompt, and Offline Sherpa as words to boost (only the words its model can spell). The older LiteRT models of Offline Whisper cannot use a list.
More words to listen for
Optional. Separate them with commas. These go first, before the words from your dictionary
Per language
Some models are better at some languages. Give a language its own model on the same server, or a server of its own. Dictation follows the language of the layout you are typing on.

Recognition uses the speech recognizer of your device. On Android 12 and later it runs on your device when the language model is installed. If it is not, the audio goes to the recognizer service while you speak. Press and hold the microphone to speak in walkie-talkie style. It stops when you let go.
Language button on the compact bar
Pick the voice typing language without leaving the bar

Adds a small button with the language code, such as EN, to the compact bar over the keys. Tap it to choose which language voice typing listens for: the keyboard\'s language, one language whatever the keyboard is set to, or all your keyboard languages at once. It is the same choice as the button on the full voice panel.\n\nThis setting is off by default, because the bar has room for one line. The button shows only when you have more than one keyboard language, or a language already chosen.
Reopen voice typing where you left it
Close the keyboard with voice typing open, and it opens listening next time

When the keyboard goes away with the voice panel, the compact bar or the collapsed bar on screen, the next text field you tap opens on the same view and starts listening.\n\nTo stop that, leave voice typing before you close the keyboard: press Back or the close button on the panel or the compact bar, the keyboard button on the collapsed bar, or the Voice tool. The keyboard then opens on the keys as usual until you start voice typing again. Password fields always open on the keys.
Pause media during voice typing
Pause music and video while the microphone listens
Microphone
Prefer a Bluetooth, wired or USB microphone when one is connected

Which microphone voice typing listens through. Automatic uses the one Android picks, which is a plugged-in headset before the phone. Pick a kind to prefer it whenever one is connected. When it is not connected, voice typing uses the automatic choice.

Offline Whisper and the transcription server can use every kind. The system recognizer records the audio itself, so for it only Bluetooth has an effect.

The microphone button on the voice panel and both voice bars shows the microphone in use. Tap it to switch to the next one that is connected.

Microphone switch
Pick the microphone, and switch it from the voice panel

On, you can choose a microphone below, and a button on the voice panel and both voice bars shows the microphone in use and switches to the next one that is connected.\n\nOff, voice typing always listens through the microphone Android picks. The keyboard does not move the audio to a headset, and the button is gone.
Recognition service
Which app does the recognising

Any app on the phone that offers speech recognition to other apps can do it here: Marmalade, Transcribro, FUTO Voice Input and the like, as well as the phone\'s own. The phone\'s default is whichever one Android has set in its own voice input settings. Prefer on-device recognition only applies to that default.
Phone\'s default
An app that is no longer installed
Prefer on-device recognition
Use the speech model on your phone when it has one for the language

On Android 12 and later the system recognizer can run on your phone when the language model is installed. If the model on the phone hears nothing at all, the keyboard switches that language to the recognizer service until the keyboard restarts.\n\nTurn this off to always use the recognizer service. That service can send the audio over the internet while you speak.
Engine for each language
Pick an engine and a model for each of your languages

Each language can use its own engine. For example, English can use the system recognizer and Bangla an Offline Whisper model. A language set to the default uses the recognition engine above.\n\nOnly the models on your phone are listed. Download more on the page of each engine.
Default (%1$s)
Engine for %1$s
Change engine from the voice tool
A chip on the voice panel picks the engine and model for the language you dictate in

Shows a chip in the bottom left corner of the voice panel. It names the engine that the language you dictate in uses. Tap it to pick another engine or model for that language. Only the models on your phone are listed. The pick is the same as the one under Engine for each language.

When voice typing starts, the keyboard asks other apps to pause their sound. Music, podcasts and video stop while the microphone listens. They continue a moment after voice typing stops. An app that ignores the request continues to play.
Tidy dictation with AI
Remove filler words, repeats and spoken corrections from each phrase

After each phrase goes into the field, the keyboard sends it to the model of the AI tool. The model removes filler words such as um and uh, false starts, repeated words and the parts that you corrected aloud: \"at three, no, four\" becomes \"at four\". Your words, language and tone stay the same. The phrase stays as you said it if the answer is slow or fails, or if you change the text first. The next phrase starts when the answer arrives. Each phrase goes to the AI provider that you set for the AI tool. Plain text mode, password fields and the boxes of the keyboard itself are not tidied.
Hold the tool to pick a mode
Press and hold the Voice tool on the toolbar to choose a voice typing mode and start at once

A press and hold on the toolbar\'s Voice tool opens a menu of the three voice typing modes. Picking one makes it the mode and starts dictation straight away, so switching between one block at a time and typing while you speak is one hold rather than a trip through settings. Tap the tool to stop. Turn this off to give the hold back to the toolbar: it then runs the tool you bound to it, or opens this screen.
Hold to talk
How long you hold the microphone before it becomes press-and-hold

A short tap on the microphone starts dictation and leaves it running until you tap again. Holding it instead dictates only while you hold, like a walkie-talkie. This is the line between the two. Raise it if a slow press keeps stopping your dictation, lower it if you mean to hold and it keeps latching on.
Voice typing language
The language dictation listens for, or several at once
Follow the keyboard
Your keyboard languages
Other languages

Following the keyboard, dictation listens for the language of the layout you are typing on. Tick one language to keep dictation in it whatever the layout. Tick several to speak any of them. The system recognizer tells them apart on Android 14 and later, where the recognizer supports it. Offline Whisper and the transcription server work out the language themselves, so give Whisper a model that covers all of them. Elsewhere the first language is the one heard: the keyboard\'s language when it is ticked.
Whistle model
Cactus Whistle

Whistle is a speech recognition model by Cactus Compute that runs on this phone. It covers English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Polish, and it is small and quick enough that a phrase is usually typed a moment after you stop. While a layout in another language is in use, dictation uses the system recognizer instead. The model comes from Hugging Face once, and after that no audio leaves the phone.
Not downloaded · %1$s
Ready. No audio leaves your phone
Asr4All models

Asr4All is an English speech recognition model that runs on this phone and listens as you speak: the words appear while you talk, and a second pass adds punctuation and capitals. Of the sizes you download, the largest is used. Small is quickest, Large the most accurate. While a layout in another language is in use, dictation uses the system recognizer instead. The models come from Hugging Face once, under their own licence, which allows dictation; after that no audio leaves the phone.
Parakeet model

Parakeet TDT is a speech recognition model by NVIDIA that runs on this phone. It transcribes 25 European languages, among them English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish, Dutch, Ukrainian and Russian, and it works out which one you speak. It is a large model, so it suits a recent phone with plenty of memory. A phrase is transcribed once you stop, and can run to 50 seconds. While a layout in another language is in use, dictation uses the system recognizer instead. The model comes from Hugging Face once, and after that no audio leaves the phone.
Moonshine model
Sherpa models

Sherpa runs k2-fsa\'s sherpa-onnx with streaming Zipformer models on this phone. The words go into the field while you speak, and the phrase ends by itself after the pause set in Stop after a pause, which Silero, a small voice detector packed with every model, listens for. Download the model for each language you dictate in; a language with no model here uses the system recognizer. Punctuation (English) adds punctuation and capitals to English phrases once it is downloaded; for other languages, turn on Add punctuation and capitals on the Voice typing screen. Sherpa also needs ONNX Runtime, a one-time download of about 33 MB. The models come from Hugging Face once, and after that no audio leaves the phone.
Punctuates English phrases
Omnilingual model

Omnilingual ASR is Meta\'s speech recognition model for more than 1,600 languages, about 380 of them keyboard languages here, many with no other voice typing. It runs on this phone through sherpa-onnx and works out the language itself. Each phrase is written out at the short pause after it, so the words arrive a phrase at a time, and dictation ends after the pause set in Stop after a pause. It is a large model: a 365 MB download that takes about 1 GB of memory while you dictate, so it suits a recent phone. It writes plain words without punctuation; Add punctuation and capitals, on the Voice typing screen, puts it in for 88 languages. Omnilingual also needs ONNX Runtime, a one-time download of about 33 MB. The model comes from Hugging Face once, and after that no audio leaves the phone.

Moonshine Tiny is a small English speech recognition model that runs on this phone. It is made for short phrases on small devices: it reads only as much audio as you said, so a short phrase is quick. A phrase is transcribed once you stop, and can run to 30 seconds. While a layout in another language is in use, dictation uses the system recognizer instead. The model comes from Hugging Face once, and after that no audio leaves the phone.

Your own models

Any streaming transducer or Paraformer model made for sherpa-onnx. It needs an encoder, a decoder and tokens.txt, and a transducer also needs its joiner. A model you bring is used before the ones listed above, for the languages you give it. Delete it to go back to them.
